fullPassage: Rescuing Cultural Treasures During World War II, there was a group of people who risked everything to protect priceless works of art from ruin. In 1943, around 345 people from 14 different Allied nations* came together to form the Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives (MFAA) program. They were not trained soldiers but scholars and experts of various kinds, such as professors, historians, and architects. These brave men and women volunteered to protect Europe’s cultural heritage and became known as the “Monuments Men.” From Preventing Destruction to Saving Treasures When the MFAA was first formed, its main goal was to prevent the destruction of cultural landmarks. The Monuments Men persuaded the Allied forces not to bomb areas with museums, churches, or other culturally significant buildings. They also visited areas that had already been destroyed to restore damaged architecture and works of art. It wasn’t long before their role expanded. During the war, the Nazis had been stealing works of art and other cultural treasures from countries across Europe. They hid these treasures in places like castles, mines, and caves. When the Monuments Men learned about this, they started looking for the stolen treasures. Their search has since been called “the greatest treasure hunt in history.” When Germany began to lose the war, the stolen objects came under threat. Hitler ordered his forces to destroy everything that could be useful to the Allied armies before they retreated from an area. Some Nazi leaders believed that this included not just military and industrial equipment but everything of value — even the stolen works of art. A Race against the Clock at Altaussee One of the largest collections of stolen items was hidden in the salt mines of Altaussee, Austria. Upon discovering its location, some of the Monuments Men rushed to the mines. They hoped to recover everything before it was too late. Meanwhile, the Nazi leader who was in charge of the area tried to destroy everything by setting off large explosives inside the mines. This could have been disastrous. Luckily, some local miners found the explosives in the mines and came up with a plan to protect their livelihood. They secretly removed the large explosives and put smaller ones at the entrances. Once they went off, the Nazi leader believed that everything was destroyed. However, while the small explosions sealed off the entrances, they left the rest of the mines and the works of art unharmed. When the Monuments Men arrived and squeezed their way into the mines, they must have been amazed to see what was inside. There were thousands of priceless objects, including paintings, statues, books, furniture, and more. The Monuments Men thought it would take about one year to transport everything they found to a safe location. However, because control of the area was going to change at the end of the war, they would have access to the mines for just two months. With insufficient packing supplies and only a few trucks, the transporting mission seemed impossible. Not only that, but food was in short supply. Even without eating proper meals, they worked up to twenty hours a day. They used coats and gas masks as packing materials and did everything they could to accomplish this vital mission in time. In the end, the Monuments Men succeeded in rescuing thousands of stolen works of art, including important pieces such as Jan van Eyck’s Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, Johannes Vermeer’s The Astronomer, and Michelangelo’s Madonna of Bruges. The Continuing Impact of the Monuments Men The efforts of the Monuments Men did not end with the war. For several years, they continued the work of recovering cultural treasures and identifying where they had been stolen from. In the end, the Monuments Men returned more than five million works of art and objects of cultural importance to their places of origin. Not everything that was stolen by the Nazis has been found, but what the Monuments Men accomplished is truly amazing. Without this determined group, the search for stolen works of art might never have begun. In addition, countless historical and cultural landmarks would have been lost forever due to the destruction of war. It is worth remembering the Monuments Men’s contribution to the preservation of cultural heritage. Thanks to their efforts, many incredible cultural sites and works of art have survived and can still be appreciated to this day.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: to forming → to form (to부정사는 to + 동사원형)

③ volunteered to protect: 'volunteered to protect Europe's cultural heritage'는 'volunteer + to부정사(~하기를 자원하다)' 구조라 to protect가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ to prevent the destruction: 'its main goal was to prevent ~'은 주격보어 자리의 to부정사(명사적 용법)라 to prevent가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: believing → believed (주절에 본동사 필요)
det.analysis:
① could have been: 'This could have been disastrous'는 '재앙이 될 수도 있었다'라는 과거 사실에 대한 추측으로 'could have + 과거분사'가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② found the explosives: 'some local miners found the explosives'는 주어(miners) 뒤의 과거형 본동사 found가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ believing that everything → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Once they went off, the Nazi leader ___ that everything was destroyed.'에서 'Once ~'는 부사절이고, 주절의 주어 the Nazi leader에는 본동사가 필요해요. 따라서 과거형 believed가 되어야 해요. 분사 believing은 본동사가 될 수 없어 문장에 동사가 사라져요. ❌ ←정답

④ must have been amazed: 'they must have been amazed'는 과거에 대한 강한 추측 'must have + 과거분사'이고, 사람이 놀라움을 느끼므로 감정분사 amazed가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 부사절(Once ~) 뒤의 주절에는 반드시 본동사가 있어야 한다 → believed

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: which → what (선행사 없는 명사절)
det.analysis:
① which the Monuments Men accomplished → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'but ___ the Monuments Men accomplished is truly amazing'에서 밑줄 부분은 is의 주어가 되는 명사절이에요. 앞에 선행사(명사)가 없으므로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what(~하는 것)을 써야 해요. which는 앞에 선행사가 있어야 하므로 틀려요. ❌ ←정답

② might never have begun: 'Without this determined group, the search ~ might never have begun'은 '~이 없었다면 시작되지 못했을 것'이라는 가정법 과거완료(might have + 과거분사)라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ would have been lost: 'countless landmarks would have been lost forever'도 같은 가정법 과거완료의 수동태(would have been + 과거분사)로 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ can still be appreciated: 'works of art ~ can still be appreciated'는 작품이 '감상되는' 대상이므로 조동사 + 수동태(can be + 과거분사)로 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 선행사(명사)가 앞에 없고 명사절 전체가 주어/목적어면 what, 선행사가 있으면 which

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: protect → destroy: 히틀러는 적에게 유용할 모든 것을 '파괴하라'고 명령
det.analysis:
✅ ① hid these treasures: 나치가 보물을 성·광산·동굴 등에 '숨겼다(hid)'는 문맥에 적절

✅ ② started looking: Monuments Men이 이를 알고 도난 보물을 '찾기 시작했다(started looking)'는 문맥에 적절

✅ ③ came under threat: 독일이 지기 시작하자 도난품이 '위협에 처했다(came under threat)'는 문맥에 적절

❌ ④ protect everything → destroy everything: 히틀러는 후퇴 전에 적군(연합군)에게 유용할 만한 모든 것을 '파괴하라(destroy)'고 명령했어요. '보호하라(protect)'는 정반대라 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 초토화 명령 문맥: destroy(파괴하다) ↔ protect(보호하다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: abandon → recover: 너무 늦기 전에 모든 것을 '되찾기를' 바람
det.analysis:
✅ ① rushed to the mines: 위치를 알아낸 Monuments Men이 광산으로 '서둘러 갔다(rushed)'는 문맥에 적절

❌ ② abandon everything → recover everything: Monuments Men은 너무 늦기 전에 모든 것을 '되찾기를(recover)' 바랐어요. 예술품을 구하려는 사람들이므로 '버리다(abandon)'는 정반대라 부적절 ←정답

✅ ③ setting off large explosives: 나치 지도자가 '폭발물을 설치하여(setting off large explosives)' 모든 것을 파괴하려 했다는 문맥에 적절

✅ ④ protect their livelihood: 지역 광부들이 자신의 '생계를 지키려는(protect their livelihood)' 계획을 세웠다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 예술품을 구하러 온 사람들: recover(되찾다) ↔ abandon(버리다)

det.korean: 빈칸에 to a safe location(안전한 장소로)이 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① to the front lines(전선으로): 예술품을 전선으로 옮긴다는 것은 보호 문맥과 반대라 부적절

❌ ② to a public market(공개 시장으로): 시장으로 옮긴다는 내용은 본문에 없고 약탈품을 파는 상황이 아니라 부적절

✅ ③ to a safe location(안전한 장소로): Monuments Men은 발견한 모든 것을 '안전한 장소로' 옮기려 했어요. 글 전체가 예술품을 지키려는 활동이고, 뒤에 제한된 시간·물자 속에서도 운반을 완수했다는 흐름이라 적절 ←정답

❌ ④ to the enemy base(적 기지로): 적 기지로 옮긴다는 것은 보호 목적과 정반대라 부적절

det.analysis:
✅ ① to their places of origin(원래 있던 곳으로): 앞 문장에서 '어디에서 도난당했는지 확인하는(identifying where they had been stolen from)' 일을 했다고 했으므로, 500만 점이 넘는 작품을 '원래 있던 곳으로' 돌려보냈다가 자연스러워요 ←정답

questions.passage: Rescuing Cultural Treasures During World War II, there was a group of people who risked everything to protect priceless works of art from ruin.  In 1943, around 345 people from 14 different Allied nations* came together to form the Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives (MFAA) program.  They were not trained soldiers but scholars and experts of various kinds, such as professors, historians, and architects.  These brave men and women volunteered to protect Europe’s cultural heritage and became known as the “Monuments Men. ” From Preventing Destruction to Saving Treasures When the MFAA was first formed, its main goal was to prevent the destruction of cultural landmarks.  The Monuments Men persuaded the Allied forces not to bomb areas with museums, churches, or other culturally significant buildings.  They also visited areas that had already been destroyed to restore damaged architecture and works of art.  It wasn’t long before their role expanded.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

② 소금 광산은 하나의 사례(Altaussee)일 뿐이고, 지질학적 이유를 다루지 않으므로 부적절

③ 전쟁이 경제에 미친 영향은 본문에 언급되지 않아 부적절

④ 글 전체가 학자·전문가로 이루어진 Monuments Men이 전쟁 중 문화유산과 예술품을 지키고 되찾은 노력과 그 의의를 소개하므로 주제로 적절 ←정답
det.tip: 세부 사례(광산·약탈)가 아니라 글 전체를 포괄하는 '문화유산을 지킨 사람들의 활동'이 주제입니다.

questions.passage: Rescuing Cultural Treasures During World War II, there was a group of people who risked everything to protect priceless works of art from ruin.  In 1943, around 345 people from 14 different Allied nations* came together to form the Monuments, Fine Arts, and Archives (MFAA) program.  They were not trained soldiers but scholars and experts of various kinds, such as professors, historians, and architects.  These brave men and women volunteered to protect Europe’s cultural heritage and became known as the “Monuments Men. ” From Preventing Destruction to Saving Treasures When the MFAA was first formed, its main goal was to prevent the destruction of cultural landmarks.  The Monuments Men persuaded the Allied forces not to bomb areas with museums, churches, or other culturally significant buildings.  They also visited areas that had already been destroyed to restore damaged architecture and works of art.  It wasn’t long before their role expanded.  During the war, the Nazis had been stealing works of art and other cultural treasures from countries across Europe.  They hid these treasures in places like castles, mines, and caves.
questions.stem: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체를 대표하는 제목.
det.analysis:
① The Monuments Men: Guardians of Art in Wartime(모뉴먼츠 맨: 전시의 예술 수호자): 전쟁 중 예술품과 문화유산을 지키고 되찾은 Monuments Men의 활동을 포괄하므로 제목으로 적절 ←정답

② How the Nazis Amassed a Vast Collection of Stolen Art(나치가 방대한 약탈 예술품을 긁어모은 방법): 나치는 약탈한 쪽이고 글의 주인공이 아니므로 부적절

③ Salt Mines: The Safest Place to Store Treasures(소금 광산: 보물을 보관하기 가장 안전한 곳): 광산은 한 사례일 뿐 글 전체를 대표하지 못해 부적절

④ The Decline of European Museums After the War(전후 유럽 박물관의 쇠퇴): 박물관의 쇠퇴는 본문에 없어 부적절
det.tip: 글의 주인공(Monuments Men)과 핵심 행위(예술 수호)를 모두 담은 제목을 고르세요.

ch: The Monuments Men: Guardians of Art in Wartime
How the Nazis Amassed a Vast Collection of Stolen Art
Salt Mines: The Safest Place to Store Treasures

questions.passage: <u>A Race against the Clock</u> at Altaussee One of the largest collections of stolen items was hidden in the salt mines of Altaussee, Austria.  Upon discovering its location, some of the Monuments Men rushed to the mines.  They hoped to recover everything before it was too late.  Meanwhile, the Nazi leader who was in charge of the area tried to destroy everything by setting off large explosives inside the mines.  This could have been disastrous.  Luckily, some local miners found the explosives in the mines and came up with a plan to protect their livelihood.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 A Race against the Clock이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 친 관용 표현이 가리키는 상황.
det.analysis:
① 경쟁자와의 쟁탈전: 다른 세력과 보물을 두고 다투는 상황이 아니라 부적절

② 한정된 시간 안에 서둘러 끝내야 하는 긴박함: 'race against the clock'은 '시간과의 싸움'이라는 관용 표현으로, 광산에 서둘러 달려가 너무 늦기 전에 모든 것을 되찾아야 하고 나치가 폭발물로 파괴하려는 위협까지 겹친 긴박한 상황을 뜻하므로 적절 ←정답

③ 느리고 정교한 복원 작업: '느림'은 시간에 쫓기는 긴박함과 반대라 부적절

④ 군사 작전의 신속한 전개: Monuments Men은 군사 작전이 아니라 예술품을 구하는 작업을 했으므로 부적절
det.tip: race against the clock = 시간과의 싸움. 바로 뒤의 'before it was too late'와 폭발물 위협이 단서입니다.

ch: 경쟁자들보다 먼저 보물을 차지하려는 치열한 쟁탈전

낡은 시계를 수리하듯 느리고 정교하게 진행하는 복원 작업

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 its가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 친 its가 가리키는 명사.
det.analysis:
① 나치 지도자가 관할하던 지역: 뒤에 등장하는 내용으로 밑줄 친 its의 선행 대상이 아니라 부적절

② Monuments Men이 결성한 프로그램: MFAA는 앞 단락의 내용으로 이 문장의 its가 가리키는 대상이 아니라 부적절

③ 소금 광산 마을: Altaussee는 광산의 위치일 뿐 its가 직접 가리키는 대상이 아니라 부적절

④ 나치가 훔쳐 숨긴 대규모 장물 수집품: 바로 앞 문장 'One of the largest collections of stolen items was hidden ~'의 '수집품'이 its의 대상이에요. 'Upon discovering its location(그것의 위치를 발견하자마자)'은 그 수집품의 위치를 가리키므로 적절 ←정답
det.tip: its 바로 앞 문장의 주어(the largest collection of stolen items)가 its가 가리키는 대상입니다.

det.korean: 빈칸에 useful to the Allied armies(연합군에게 유용한)가 적절
det.analysis:

❌ ② sold to foreign collectors(외국 수집가에게 팔린): 파괴 명령 문맥과 무관해 부적절

✅ ③ useful to the Allied armies(연합군에게 유용한): 히틀러는 후퇴 전에 적군(연합군)에게 '유용할' 만한 모든 것을 파괴하라고 명령했어요. 뒤 문장의 '군사·산업 장비(military and industrial equipment)'가 단서라 적절 ←정답

❌ ④ returned to its true owners(진짜 주인에게 돌려준): 파괴를 명령하는 문맥과 정반대라 부적절
det.tip: destroy everything that could be ___(파괴하라) + 뒤의 'military and industrial equipment' 단서 → 적군(연합군)에게 유용한

questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'그들은 코트와 방독면을 포장 재료로 사용했다.'

[조건]
(1) and, as, coats, gas, masks, materials, packing, They, used 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 코트와 방독면을 포장 재료로 사용했다는 문장.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- They(주어): 그들은
- used(동사) + coats and gas masks(목적어): 코트와 방독면을 사용했다
- as packing materials(부사구): 포장 재료로서
- 'use A as B(A를 B로 사용하다)' 구문으로, as는 '~로서'의 뜻을 나타내요.
det.tip: use A as B = A를 B로(서) 사용하다 → used coats and gas masks as packing materials

questions.wa: They used coats and gas masks as packing materials

questions.passage: In the end, the Monuments Men succeeded in __________ (rescue) thousands of stolen works of art. The Continuing Impact of the Monuments Men The efforts of the Monuments Men did not end with the war.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: '~하는 데 성공했다(succeed in -ing)'가 되도록 rescue를 변형.
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'succeed in + 동명사(V-ing)'는 '~하는 데 성공하다'라는 표현이에요. 전치사 in 뒤에는 명사나 동명사가 와야 하므로 동사 rescue를 동명사 rescuing으로 바꿔야 해요: succeeded in rescuing(구조하는 데 성공했다).
det.tip: 전치사 in 뒤에는 동명사(-ing) → succeed in rescuing

questions.passage: These brave men and women volunteered to protect Europe’s cultural heritage and became known as the “Monuments Men. ” From Preventing Destruction to Saving Treasures When the MFAA was first formed, its main goal was to prevent the destruction of cultural landmarks.  __________ with museums, churches, or other culturally significant buildings.  They also visited areas that had already been destroyed to restore damaged architecture and works of art.  It wasn’t long before their role expanded. questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'Monuments Men은 연합군에게 (특정) 지역을 폭격하지 말라고 설득했다.'

[조건]
(1) Allied, areas, bomb, forces, Men, Monuments, not, persuaded, the, The, to 를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 11단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 연합군에게 지역을 폭격하지 말라고 설득했다는 문장.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- The Monuments Men(주어) + persuaded(동사) + the Allied forces(목적어): 연합군을 설득했다
- not to bomb areas(목적격보어): 지역을 폭격하지 말라고
- 'persuade + 목적어 + to부정사'는 '~에게 …하라고 설득하다'이고, 부정은 to 앞에 not을 붙여 'not to + 동사원형'으로 만들어요.
det.tip: persuade + 목적어 + (not) to부정사. 부정은 to 바로 앞에 not → persuaded the Allied forces not to bomb

questions.wa: The Monuments Men persuaded the Allied forces not to bomb areas
accept: The Monuments Men persuaded the Allied forces not to bomb areas

questions.passage: This could have been disastrous.  Luckily, some local miners found the explosives in the mines and came up with a plan to protect their livelihood.  __________.  Once they went off, the Nazi leader believed that everything was destroyed.  However, while the small explosions sealed off the entrances, they left the rest of the mines and the works of art unharmed.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 [보기]에 주어진 단어를 모두 올바른 순서로 배열하시오. (13단어, 영어로)

'그들은 큰 폭발물을 몰래 치우고 더 작은 것들을 입구에 두었다.'

[단어] and / at / entrances / explosives / large / ones / put / removed / secretly / smaller / the / the / They

det.korean: 큰 폭발물을 치우고 작은 것들을 입구에 두었다는 문장.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- They(주어) + secretly(부사) + removed the large explosives(동사구1): 큰 폭발물을 몰래 치웠다
- and(등위접속사): 두 동사구를 병렬 연결
- put smaller ones at the entrances(동사구2): 더 작은 것들을 입구에 두었다
- 하나의 주어에 removed와 put 두 과거동사가 and로 병렬된 구조예요.
det.tip: 주어(They) + removed ~ and put ~ : 과거동사 두 개를 and로 병렬하세요.

questions.wa: They secretly removed the large explosives and put smaller ones at the entrances
accept: They secretly removed the large explosives and put smaller ones at the entrances

questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'그들은 문화재를 회수하는 일을 계속했다.'

det.korean: 문화재를 회수하는 일을 계속했다는 문장.
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- they(주어) + continued(동사) + the work(목적어): 그 일을 계속했다
- of recovering cultural treasures(전치사구): 문화재를 회수하는
- 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 recovering을 써서 'the work of recovering(회수하는 일)'이 돼요.
det.tip: the work of + 동명사 = ~하는 일 → the work of recovering cultural treasures

questions.wa: they continued the work of recovering cultural treasures
accept: they continued the work of recovering cultural treasures
